title: Rounds in flight stay tracers; modelled ammunition where it is stationary or under the camera; the Rotor ejects brass in sentry control
context: The bullet study brief (relayed from the owner's other session): the workshop's ammunition library ships round, projectile and case forms per family at game and display tiers; neither the Rotor nor the Needle should fly modelled bullets; produce a per-weapon verdict with costs and hook points and prototype one visible win, probably Rotor brass ejection in sentry control. Library head 8ae723d for pinning.
outcome: docs/AMMUNITION.md is the verdict: Rotor and Needle stay tracers in flight (sub-pixel on the sphere); the Rotor's case ejects in sentry control and a round belt is the later diegetic count; a modelled needle50 only for chambering, slow motion or a magazine readout; the mortar81 projectile is a one-for-one replacement for the derived olive shell; tank_arrow and tank_dart rounds fit the MORK's nine ammo ports as the readout; the Quiver's kit missiles are already the one flying mesh that earns it. Prototype: rotor_light_case_game pinned in docs/ammunition-assets.lock.json; src/fx/brass.js instances it in a pool of 48 with velocity, spin, gravity toward the centre, rest on the rock roof and a shrink-out; the tower fire site ejects one per Rotor round when the camera is within eight cells; the acceptance asserts live brass during the Rotor kill.
alternatives: Model the Rotor's projectile: rejected, 22 triangles that are sub-pixel and were already mistaken for sparks.
A physics body per case: rejected, an instanced pool with a radial gravity and a roof stop is all the eye needs.
evidence: npm test 93, npm run check (ammunition lock verified)
browser --story-world with the brass assertion before commit
